Drawing on a sociological reading, they contend that rejection of an incumbent does not imply confidence in the alternative, so voters may punish Republicans without endorsing Democratic policy. They trace a pattern since 2016 in which negative voting, motivated by fear of the opponent, has mobilised voters more effectively than loyalty to a programme. This dynamic weakens parties' incentives to respond to internal criticism and risks mistaking electoral victory for approval of every policy. They contend that in her work the cables become oppressive blade-like structures that shape movement and existence in the city, and that architecture is defined by the void they leave.
